decisions.risk.production: High risk: the task touches production.
decisions.risk.destructive: High risk: the task is destructive.
decisions.risk.external: High risk: the task has external side effects (push, publish, send, deploy).
decisions.risk.remote_irreversible: High risk: the task touches a remote system and cannot be reversed.
decisions.risk.remote: Medium risk: the task touches a remote system.
decisions.risk.irreversible: Medium risk: the task is not reversible.
decisions.risk.many_files: Medium risk: about {files} files are touched (more than 5).
decisions.risk.untested: Medium risk: several files are touched and there are no tests.
decisions.risk.low: Low risk: no risk rule fired.
decisions.complexity.trivial: Trivial: at most one file, no unknowns, a single piece of work.
decisions.complexity.simple: Simple: at most 3 files and at most 1 unknown ({files} files, {unknowns} unknowns).
decisions.complexity.moderate: Moderate: at most 10 files and at most 3 unknowns ({files} files, {unknowns} unknowns).
decisions.complexity.complex: Complex: more than 10 files or more than 3 unknowns ({files} files, {unknowns} unknowns).
decisions.uncertainty: Uncertainty {value} from open questions and missing tests.
decisions.strategy.plan_mode: Plan mode: investigate and plan only.
decisions.strategy.gated: High risk: approval is required before the impactful step.
decisions.strategy.direct: Low risk and small: act directly with proportional checks.
decisions.strategy.review: An independent review is required (medium or high risk, or complex work).
decisions.eval.status: The task status is {status}, not verified.
decisions.eval.no_tested: No evidence item is labeled as tested.
decisions.eval.failing: {count} command evidence item(s) have a non-zero exit code.
decisions.esc.few: No failed attempt yet: keep going.
decisions.esc.keep: Failures so far do not repeat and are below half the attempt limit.
decisions.esc.repeat: The same error repeated in the last two failures ({signature}): the next attempt runs on a stronger model.
decisions.esc.limit: {count} failed attempt(s) reached half the limit of {limit}: the next attempt runs on a stronger model.
decisions.esc.ask_human: {count} failed attempts used the whole limit of {limit}: only a person can reopen the task.
decisions.jev.why.env_file_insecure: the file {path} can be read by other users; run chmod 600 {path}
decisions.jev.unavailable: JEV was unavailable ({why}); the local policy was used.
decisions.jev.floor: The local policy rates the risk as {local}, higher than JEV ({jev}); the higher level was kept.
decisions.error.negative_signal: files_touched_estimate and unknowns must not be negative.
decisions.error.no_agents: No agents are available to route the task to.
decisions.error.no_verdicts: At least one verdict is required to resolve a conflict.
models.base.high_risk: Premium tier: the task is high risk.
models.base.complex: Premium tier: the task is complex.
models.base.economy: Economy tier: low risk and trivial.
models.base.standard: Standard tier: the default for everything else.
models.escalated: Attempt {attempt}: moved up to the {tier} tier after repeated failures.
models.clamped: The agent's tier bounds moved the choice to the {tier} tier.
models.pinned_unavailable: The pinned model {model} is unavailable; selecting by tier.
models.tier_unavailable: Every model in the {tier} tier is unavailable.
models.error.bounds: Tier bounds are inverted: minimum {low} is above maximum {high}.
models.error.none_available: No model is available within the allowed tiers.
decide.signals.help: Path to a JSON file with task signals.
decide.remote.help: The task touches a remote system.
decide.external.help: The task has external side effects (push, publish, send, deploy).
decide.no_tests.help: The affected code has no tests.
decide.classify.help: Classify a task: complexity, risk and uncertainty.
decide.strategy.help: Classify a task and select the execution strategy.
decide.route_model.help: Classify a task and select a model.
decide.attempt.help: Number of the current attempt, starting at 0.
decide.unavailable.help: A model id that is unavailable (repeatable).
decide.agent_model.help: Concrete model id pinned by the agent.
decide.error.no_objective: Provide --objective or a signals file that contains one.
decisions.jev.distrusted: JEV answer for {question} was not trusted (low confidence or uncertain); the local value {value} was used.
decisions.jev.why.binary_missing: binary not found or not executable
decisions.jev.why.not_on_path: program {program} was not found on the allowed path (permissions.exec_path). Fix it by setting decision.jev.command to the program's absolute path, or by adding its directory to permissions.exec_path
decisions.jev.why.not_a_file: program {program} was not found as an executable regular file. Fix it by setting decision.jev.command to the program's absolute path, or by adding its directory to permissions.exec_path and naming it without a path
decisions.jev.warning: decision.provider is jev but the program does not resolve, so the local policy is used: {why}
decisions.jev.why.in_run_root: program {program} is inside the run root, which the agent can write
decisions.strategy.no_plan: No plan step: act directly with proportional checks.
decisions.plan.forced: Executor tier {tier}, planning {planning}: plan mode and gated flows always have a plan, whatever the tier.
decisions.plan.always: Executor tier {tier}, planning always: a plan is required by configuration.
decisions.plan.never: Executor tier {tier}, planning never: the plan step is skipped by configuration.
decisions.plan.auto.economy: Executor tier {tier}, planning auto: a plan for anything above trivial, or above low risk. With executor_tier auto only trivial low-risk tasks are routed to economy, and those need no plan, so this rule has an effect only when the tier is set explicitly.
decisions.plan.auto.standard: Executor tier {tier}, planning auto: a plan from moderate complexity up, or above low risk. With executor_tier auto this tier rule currently changes nothing for non-trivial tasks: the router gives them the standard or premium tier, which share one threshold.
decisions.plan.auto.premium: Executor tier {tier}, planning auto: a plan only from moderate complexity up, or above low risk; small tasks skip it. With executor_tier auto this tier rule currently changes nothing for non-trivial tasks: the router gives them the standard or premium tier, which share one threshold.
decide.executor_tier.help: Executor tier to assume instead of the configured or routed one (economy, standard, premium). With harness.executor_tier auto the tier currently changes the plan decision for no non-trivial task (standard and premium share a threshold); set a tier to see a difference.
decisions.floor.hit: The objective mentions '{term}': the signal {signal} is raised whatever the flags say.
decisions.risk.credentials: Medium risk: the task touches credentials or secrets.
decisions.risk.data_schema: Medium risk: the task changes a database or a schema.
decisions.jev.complexity_floor: The local policy rates the complexity as {local}, higher than JEV ({jev}); the higher level was kept.
decisions.tools.error.tokens: Tool {name}: approx_definition_tokens must be a non-negative integer.
decisions.tools.floor.read: {tool} kept: a read tool the agent already had (floor).
decisions.tools.floor.edit: {tool} kept: the task changes files and the agent may change them (floor).
decisions.tools.floor.shell: {tool} kept: the task has checks to run (floor).
decisions.tools.floor.all: {tool} kept: the agent has none of the read tools, so its whole tool list is the floor.
decisions.tools.floor.enforced: {tool} kept: it is in the floor, which no selection can drop.
decisions.tools.lean: Left out by the lean tool profile: {tools}.
decisions.tools.refused: Ignored, because a selection can only narrow the agent's allowed tools: {tools}.
decisions.tools.invalid.profile: the profile was neither structured nor lean
decisions.tools.invalid.names: the selection was not a list of tool names
decisions.tools.fallback: The tool selection from {source} was not usable ({why}); the local policy was used.
decisions.tools.kept_all: The tool selection was not usable ({why}); the agent's whole tool list was kept.
decisions.tools.local.network: {tool} added: the task mentions '{term}' (documentation, research, URLs, APIs or upgrade notes).
decisions.tools.local.remote: {tool} added: the task mentions '{term}' (a remote system) and the agent may use remote systems.
decisions.tools.local.shell: {tool} added: the task mentions running a command ('{term}').
decisions.tools.local.dropped: {tool} dropped: nothing in the task asks for it.
decisions.tools.jev.kept: {tool} kept: JEV answered {value} for 'needed', above the drop threshold of {threshold}.
decisions.tools.jev.dropped: {tool} dropped: JEV answered {value} for 'needed', at or below the drop threshold of {threshold}.
decisions.tools.jev.floor: Floor tools were not asked about and are kept: {tools}.
decisions.tools.jev.profile_distrusted: JEV's tool profile answer was not trusted (low confidence); the locally resolved profile {value} was kept.
decisions.tools.jev.too_many: {count} tools to ask about is more than the limit of {limit} questions; the local policy was used.
decisions.tools.jev.nothing: Every candidate tool is in the floor, so there was nothing to ask JEV; the local policy was used.
decisions.tools.contract: Tools for this task: {selected}. Left out for this task: {dropped}. If you needed one that was left out, stop and say so in your report; it can be restored with 'wev task tools {task} --add TOOL --reason TEXT'.
decisions.tools.contract_all: Tools for this task: {selected}. None of your tools was left out.
decisions.tools.restored: Tool {tool} restored for task {task} (a selection miss): {reason}
decisions.tools.error.no_selection: Task {task} has no tool selection (harness.tool_selection is off for this run), so there is nothing to restore.
decisions.tools.error.not_running: Task {task} is {status}; a tool can be restored only while the task is running.
decisions.tools.error.not_offered: Tool {tool} is outside the tools agent {agent} is allowed, so it cannot be restored.
decisions.tools.error.already: Tool {tool} is already selected for task {task}.
decisions.tools.error.reason: Restoring a tool requires a reason.
decisions.tools.report.estimate: **Estimated definition tokens (approximate):** offered {offered}, selected {selected}. These are rough constants, not measurements.
orch.task.tools.help: Restore a tool that tool selection dropped for a running task; only a tool the agent is allowed, and counted as a selection miss.
orch.arg.tool_add: The tool to restore (for example Write).
orch.arg.tool_reason: Why the task needs the tool (recorded as a decision).
decide.select_tools.help: Print the tools one task needs from one agent's tool list (local policy, or the configured provider when harness.tool_selection is provider). Nothing is stored.
decide.task_file.help: Path to a JSON file holding one plan task (id, title, objective and optional fields).
decide.agent.help: Id of the agent whose tool list is narrowed.
decide.tier.help: Executor tier used to resolve tool_profile auto (default: the tier of the agent's model, else standard).
